title: BrahMos Exports Widen in Southeast Asia as Philippines Seeks More Systems
excerpt: The Philippines has taken delivery and Vietnam has signed, while talks with other Southeast Asian nations are at an advanced stage and still await government clearance, reporting says.
body:
• BrahMos Aerospace has supplied missiles to the Philippines and signed an agreement with Vietnam, according to reporting summarising Hindustan Times; talks with several other Southeast Asian nations are at an advanced stage.
  • Those pending deals still await government clearance — interest and talks are not the same as signed contracts.
  • Separately, Reuters reported the Philippines is in final-stage talks to buy about five more BrahMos systems and nearly 60 missiles, worth an estimated $700 million to $800 million.
  • India announced supply of BrahMos missiles to Indonesia in July and has also held talks with the UAE, Thailand, South Africa and Brazil, Reuters reported.

Export interest in the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile is widening across Southeast Asia. BrahMos Aerospace has supplied missiles to the Philippines and signed an agreement with Vietnam, and talks with several other Southeast Asian countries are at an advanced stage, though deals with interested countries await government clearance. Demand rose after Operation Sindoor, according to reporting that summarises a Hindustan Times account of the programme.

BrahMos is developed and manufactured by BrahMos Aerospace, the India-Russia joint venture between India's Defence Research and Development Organisation and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya. It is among the world's fastest cruise missiles and can be launched from land, sea and air platforms.

What is confirmed, and what is still in talks

The status differs by country, and the distinction matters. The Philippines is the established buyer: it signed a $375 million contract in January 2022 for shore-based anti-ship systems, becoming the first foreign customer, and deliveries under that deal are nearing completion. Vietnam is reported as a signed agreement. Indonesia was announced by Delhi in July as a supply recipient. For several other Southeast Asian nations, the reported status is advanced talks, not signed deals, and finalisation depends on government clearance.

The Hindustan Times-summarised account also described reliability testing behind the export push: missiles manufactured 10, 15 and 20 years ago were taken from stock and fired, and were reported to have performed as intended, with non-destructive testing used to verify reliability. That account did not disclose the number of missiles supplied in the latest arrangements or their financial value.

Philippines seeks a much larger second purchase

The clearest measure of the new interest is in Manila. India is in final-stage talks to expand sales to the Philippines, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters. The Philippines is expected to buy about five BrahMos systems and nearly 60 missiles in a deal potentially worth $700 million to $800 million, two Indian sources said — well above the $375 million 2022 order.

"Manila has shown interest again to procure about five systems of the BrahMos and they now view India as a very reliable partner."

— Indian source, speaking to Reuters

Philippines defence ministry spokesperson Arsenio Andolong told Reuters that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr had expressed his desire to acquire additional BrahMos missiles. Speaking virtually at the Delhi Defence Dialogue, Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said Manila hoped to secure more BrahMos units and had shared a wish list with Indian authorities to tailor the system to the Philippine environment. Reuters noted that neither India's defence and foreign ministries nor BrahMos Aerospace responded to requests for comment on that proposed expansion, and no final contract for the additional systems has been publicly announced.

Why buyers in the region want it

Manila is modernising its military and strengthening coastal defences as tensions rise with Beijing over overlapping claims in the South China Sea, where the two countries have clashed in recent years. Interest in BrahMos also increased after India used the system in battle for the first time during last year's four-day conflict with Pakistan, Reuters reported.

For India, the sales are part of a broader defence-export push. Government data cited by Reuters put India's defence exports for the fiscal year to March at 384.24 billion rupees ($4.11 billion), up more than 62 percent from the same period the year before. Beyond Southeast Asia, India is in talks on BrahMos with the UAE, Thailand, South Africa and Brazil. Which of the advanced-stage Southeast Asian talks convert into contracts will depend on the government clearances that reporting says are still pending.
